newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Uganda seeks foreign investment in oil sector.
newsitem.headline: Uganda seeks foreign investment in oil sector.

text.p: Uganda has launched a drive to attract foreign investment for what officials say are promising oil prospects on the border with strife-torn Zaire.

The country's Commissioner of Petroleum Exploration and Production, Reuben Kashambuzi told an African Oil Trade Conference the government invited foreign companies to explore for oil at three sites with a total area of about 18,000 square kilometres around the Lake Albert area.
A British company, Heritage Oil and Gas, was earlier this year granted a licence to search for oil at another site.

"The competition for risk dollars has intensified (and) this coupled with the oil price uncertainties and the frontier nature of Uganda's petroleum, called for a re-think of our promotion strategy," Kashambuzi told a session on oil exploration in Uganda.
Officials blame the slow pace of the East African nation's oil search -- now 72 years old -- on lack of seismic data, low oil prices and competition for investment from Eastern Europe.
To lure investors, Kashambuzi said Uganda is calling for regional cooperation including assistance from the 12-member Southern African Development Community.
Uganda, for its part, would improve the human and physical infrastructure needed by foreigners and offer tax incentives.
